question: Do DAF sponsors appear as holders of escheated property owed to charities? Use only state unclaimed-property bulk files that robots.txt and terms allow (California SCO publishes a statewide CSV, but its robots.txt disallows ClaudeBot, so a human or a permitted route must download it). Count records whose holder is Fidelity Investments Charitable Gift Fund, National Philanthropic Trust, Donor Advised Charitable Giving, Vanguard Charitable Endowment Program, AEF, NCF or a top-20 community foundation, by property type and year (2021+). Run no searches through state claim forms
conclusion_affected: Whether voided DAF grant checks are in practice reported as unclaimed property (sponsor liability; uncashed-grant handling)
rationale: The statutes read (RUUPA, DE, CA, NY, MA, WA) cover nonprofit holders, but no sponsor document, 990 text or enforcement record mentions escheat of grant checks. Holder-name counts in a bulk file are the only public test of practice, and California's 3-year §1520 catch-all is the broadest of the four states

question: Obtain the TPI 2026 Study of the Philanthropic Conversation full report and methodology without submitting TPI's download form: look for copies hosted publicly by the co-sponsors (DAFgiving360, Foundation Source) or the Boston Foundation, or in trade-press attachments. Confirm the sample (300 advisers / 103 HNW clients), fieldwork dates (Dec 2025-Jan 2026), screening and weighting, and the 32% vs 9% 'not enough money' pair, which the public release does not show
conclusion_affected: What the DAF industry believes that may be wrong; perception-gap metric
rationale: The DAFRC report is now verified first-hand, but its '61% vs 6%' line cites the 2018 U.S. Trust/TPI study. TPI's 2026 release confirms 90%, 96%, 78%, 51%, 73%, 85% and tax 21% vs 40%. The sample sizes and the 9% client figure rest on InvestmentNews only, and the full report sits behind a form this mission may not submit

question: Map sanctioned delegated-access routes in top-20 sponsor documents (GS DAF agent authorization, JCF Appointment of Authorized Party, Fidelity Authorized Interested Party, Vanguard Authorized Person, GKCCF/Greater Horizons 'Authorized Use', BofA Authorized Advisor form). Read the public forms only, and record for each whether a firm or software service (not only a named individual) can be appointed, what data and actions it gets, and whether credentials are shared or issued separately
conclusion_affected: Agent-access feasibility; whether a compliant agent path exists without credential sharing
rationale: The top-20 census shows that bans on credential sharing and bots coexist with documented human delegation routes. GS DAF lets 'another third party' act as agent, and JCF lets 'professional advisors' see fund data online. Whether these routes can admit a software agent decides if any compliant agentic integration is possible without a sponsor API
